description.narrative: (Zambia): The Luangwa Livelihood and Conservation (LLC) activity aims to enhance the resilience and health of natural resource-dependent ecological and human communities in the Luangwa Valley of Zambia. The valley is home to Zambia's only black rhino population and its largest elephant population. The Activity will harness over $10 million in private financing and contribute to strengthening disincentives for illegal activities, while increasing incentives to realize tangible improvements for conservation and human wellbeing. With FY 2022 funding, local communities will benefit from Maternal and Child Health interventions focused on capacity building of community health workers to address household and community level factors that delay or prevent women from seeking ante-natal care or delivery at healthcare facilities. The LLC will also increase access to safe drinking water through provision of basic water supply services such as boreholes. The activity will provide training, supplies and equipment such as communication aids, vehicles, uniforms, and rations to Wildlife Police Officers and Community Scouts to undertake effective resource protection operations. In addition, support will improve strategic law enforcement coordination among law enforcement agencies. The activity will support the development of livelihood hubs which will serve as community centers for stimulating economic opportunities for over 100,000 beneficiaries. Farmers will receive support for market access, training and mentoring in improved agricultural techniques, and farming techniques for new crops (chili, honey) to promote improved food security. Together these cross-cutting outcomes will lead to improved wellbeing of communities in the Luangwa valley and subsequently improved state of biodiversity. The LLC supports Development Objective 2 and 3 of the CDCS and will contribute to the U.S. foreign policy priority of working with partner countries to help improve their business environment..
